Mastek Limited 
Q2FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
October 26, 2026 
 
Moderator  
 
Ladies and gentlemen. Good day. Welcome to Mastek Q2FY27 Earnings call. We will begin today's 
session with a presentation from Mastek's management team, followed by a Q&A segment. I'll now 
hand the conference over to Mr. Niraj Khemka. Over to you, Mr. Niraj. 
 
Niraj Khemka 
 
Thank you, Melissa. Hello, everyone. Welcome to Mastek Limited's Q2FY27 earnings call. In the call 
today, we have with us Mr. Umang Nahata, CEO, and Mr. Deepak Kedia, CFO. In the course of this 
call, we'll make certain statements which are forward-looking and may involve a number of risks and 
uncertainties. All forward-looking statements made herein are based on information presently 
available to the management, and the company does not undertake to update any forward-looking 
statement that may be made in the course of this call. In this regard, there is full disclosure included 
in the investor presentation and the press release. We consider that as read. With this, I'll hand over 
the call to Umang. Over to you, Umang. 
 
Umang Nahata 
 
Good morning, everyone. Thank you, Niraj. 
 
First of all, very good morning, everyone, and I appreciate you all joining the call early in the morning 
today. Looking forward to a healthy interaction with all of you over the next one hour. Our Q2 
performance has been pretty healthy and very close to expectations in terms of most of the 
parameters. From a revenue standpoint, we had a very healthy growth of 2.4% QoQ in constant 
currency terms. The revenue numbers landed at $107.3 million for Q2. The EBITDA performance 
landed at 14.4%, which was around 100 basis points below Q1, largely on account of salary hike, 
and we will discuss the details later in the call. Our order backlog, 12-month order backlog grew by 
2.3% YoY. There was some softness in the order book, and we'll talk about that also as we go forward 
in the call. Overall, from a performance standpoint, I'll initially describe the performance from a geo 
standpoint. We'll then really spend time talking about how are we transforming Mastek into an AI 
native organization and some of the really interesting stuff that is going on there. And we'll later pass 
the call to Deepak to explain more on the financial performance in detail. 
 

As far as our geographical performance is concerned, from a UK standpoint, Q2 was a very robust 
quarter. We actually delivered a 4.1% revenue growth in the quarter. Financial Services continues to 
be a very strong subsector within the UK business. Our Financial Services grew by more than 16% in 
the quarter. And we continue to see good, healthy momentum in that sector. Public sector, which is 
our biggest sector in the UK-Europe geography, continues to be stable. We saw a decent growth in 
public sector, both supported by some growth momentum as well as higher working days in last 
quarter. Healthcare & Life Sciences, which was a key driver and continues to be a key growth driver 
for us, still is lagging behind in the quarter performance, primarily due to some right-shifting in project 
starts, as well as some order book. Although, having said that, I would be happy to report that some 
of these orders that were right shifted have been concluded post the close of the quarter. And we 
expect the numbers to start improving as we go forward in H2. 
 
The other important development from a UK-Europe point of view is opening up of a new front, which 
is around energy and utilities. Happy to report that we've landed three new frameworks in energy and 
utilities and also started landing new contracts within these frameworks. This is primarily aligned to 
our strategy of going after sectors which buy like public sector but operate like private sector or 
privately held organizations. And that has allowed us to open a new front in energy and utility as well. 
 
We continue to focus with our same strategy of going after arm's length bodies who buy like public 
sector kind of organizations. As we go forward in the year, we'll report progress on how is the Energy 
& Utility sector really building up as we go forward. Last and not the least, the UK also saw a change 
in prime minister last quarter. As the new ministers take over, we are expecting and watching the 
change of policy or any direction, if any, from them. It currently seems that while healthcare will 
continue to be a focus, social care might be another area of important focus for the government, and 
we are trying to make sure that we align back to the policies. The budgets for the new government 
are going to be announced anytime this week, and we are closely observing the developments there. 
 
Till some of these activities happened, few of the contracts that were to be decided have been put 
on hold or canceled, these are the orders in pipeline, and would be hopefully launched back after the 
budgets have been finalized, which resulted in a softer quarter from an order book standpoint for our 
UK business in Q2. 
 
Moving forward to North America, our North America business continues to see a very strong deal 
momentum. And we, again, this quarter had a very positive order book. In fact, our total order backlog 
for the geography, if you do a year-on-year comparison, has grown by more than 50%. These order 
bookings are both in terms of focus on key verticals, which is around Healthcare & Life sciences, 
retail and manufacturing. But a lot of AI native transformation deals are also happening in the 
geography. And we'll talk about some of them in the following slides as I go forward. 
 
On APAC and Middle East point of view specifically, as you all know, the uncertainty in the market 
continues. In fact, it is getting more stringer as we go forward. While in Q2, we had some of the old 
standing contracts being signed and therefore a decent bounce back in revenue there. However, the 
overall outlook for Middle East continues to be uncertain. And we are closely observing the situation, 
especially the situation that is unfolding in Saudi Arabia and making the right and judicious calls as 

we go forward. 
 
As I move forward and explain our business from the most important forward-looking lens, which is 
the lens of how is Mastek transforming itself to become an AI-native organization. Like I mentioned, 
our vision is to focus on transformative business and make Mastek a leader in AI transformation in 
our select-focused verticals that we operate in. In account of that focus, we have taken two really 
important new steps, new offerings that we have been working on for the last few months and which 
have launched in this quarter. 
 
First is around Healthcare & Life Sciences, where we have signed a very strategic partnership with a 
company called Innovaccer. Innovaccer is a market leader in providing contextual data in Healthcare 
& Life Sciences domain. And we will be partnering with Innovaccer as one of their largest partners 
globally to help transform Healthcare & Life Sciences businesses on the back of the contextual data 
platform that Innovaccer provides. We believe this partnership will be very strategic in positioning 
Mastek and Innovaccer as one of the leading providers of AI transformation services in Healthcare & 
Life Sciences globally. The partnership has immediately started ramping up also, including 
development of good pipe in the first quarter of its signature itself. 
 
The second important part was around Service-as-a-software. Again, this is one area that Mastek 
has been working on in the backgrounds. With our experience in enterprise applications, especially 
around Oracle and Salesforce, as well as our strong engineering and data domain, we have now been 
able to combine all the three into a new offering, which we're calling Service-as-a-software. It 
primarily has two angles. It is more about process transformation, but it can also do a lot of 
replacement of traditional SaaS softwares with new Service-as-a-software solution. In fact, Mastek 
internally, we've switched our CRM software, we've switched our procurement software, we've 
switched our recruitment system, as well as our accounts payable and expense systems on the 
same model, delivering not just good savings in our subscription cost, but also tremendous 
upliftment in terms of the way AI native solutions are being used and improving business outcomes 
and quality of performance. As we launch these learnings into the market, we've already closed our 
first few deals on Service-as-a-software, and we are seeing good momentum as we go forward. 
 
The last part of the area, again, which we call as AI Foundation, which includes governance and 
security, roadmapping, et cetera, is the third part of the business, which is also taking care well. 
Cyber was an important component that we thought we should add to our AI foundation. And we've 
been working on it over the last few months with some investments within our public sector market. 
And again, I'm very happy to report that the investments have started bearing results. And this quarter, 
again, we saw our first few significant wins in the Cyber for AI space. In our public sector deals and 
I'll talk about some of these deals in the next slide. 
 
Overall our AI momentum continues to be very strong more than 40% of our deals even in this quarter 
are AI deals and these deals are really helping shape Mastek towards the future of becoming a Data 
and AI organization, which we are doing not just for our customers but we are also internally shifting 
Mastek, as I had explained earlier. 

 
I'll now share some experiences of what kind of deals that we are seeing and some of the learning or 
references that we are creating so that investors can better understand the kind of work that is 
happening. 
 
The first example here is senior care skilled nursing facility. This is a Service-as-a-software deal out 
of North America, a multi-million dollar transaction where we are replacing the core SaaS platform 
of a skilled nursing facility and helping them develop AI native SaaS platform, which will have 
contextual data alignment and aims at delivering a significant business outcome for our client in that 
region. 
 
The second deal is a life sciences company, again, in dental technologies. This is, again, an America's 
deal where we've used AI-led productivity improvements to replace an incumbent. And it's a 10 
million plus transaction, another large deal for North America in this quarter, where we are delivering 
AI-led productivity solutions to the client to help them improve their cost of IT services while 
delivering more value to that particular organization. 
 
The third deal that you see here is the UK central government deal. Now, this is a cybersecurity deal 
that I was talking about where we are delivering cyber solutions and cyber assurance for public 
sector customer in the UK. Again, it's a multi-year contract, multi-million dollar in setup, and allows 
us to deliver cyber assurance, specifically cyber assurance even covering beyond the regular kind of 
cyber activities to our client. 
 
Similarly, the fourth deal is a process transformation deal, again, on the Oracle platform for a police 
department in UK, and where we are delivering a lot of the AI-agentic solutions that Oracle has to 
offer. In terms of delivering process transformation for a police department in UK. Also, the 
methodology that we use for these fixed-bid projects is called ADOPT AI, which is our platform for 
delivering fixed-bid projects from a process transformation standpoint. 
 
There are a couple of other deals. Again, this is a managed services deal. The next one, again, AI 
productivity, where we've been able to replace an incumbent with an aggressive AI productivity 
offering. Again, using our ADOPT AI platform, delivering a significant outcome-based managed 
services contract to the client. 
 
The last deal is in APAC and Middle East, which is again, delivering Healthcare & Life Sciences 
process transformation for a strategic healthcare partner in the region, where we are helping them 
modernize their legacy application to an AI native solution going forward. 
 
As you can see, the nature of these deals span across AI productivity, AI for transformation, Service-
as-a-software, and a few around AI foundation, which is from cyber to governance, et cetera. 
 
All of these deals give us good confidence that the three core pillars of our AI offering from AI 
Transformation to AI Foundation and then AI Productivity are all gaining good traction. And they're 

not only in some cases helping us win net-new, but also in many cases helping us deliver outcome-
based business contracts to our clients. The direction of travel, in general, we feel is very positive. 
And we're moving actively towards transforming Mastek into an AI-native organization. 
 
With that, I'll pass over the call to Deepak to share more details around the financial performance for 
the quarter. 
 
Deepak Kedia 
 
Thank you, Umang. A very warm welcome to everyone on the call, and thank you for taking the time 
to attend Mastek's earnings call so early in the morning. I'll start with a quarter’s update before 
providing updates on other matrices and some key changes on investor data sheet. 
 
In Q2, we reported revenue of $107.3 million, sequentially up by 2.4% and an operating EBITDA of 
14.4%. On a constant currency basis, revenue had a robust sequential growth of 2.4%. In rupee 
terms, we crossed four digits for the first time and reported a revenue of Rs. 1,018.7 crore, a 
sequential growth of 3.4% and a YoY growth of 8.3%. We reported PAT of 105.7 crore, or 10.3% of 
the total income. We closed the quarter with a 12-month backlog of $286.2 million, a sequential 
decline of 7.7%, and YoY growth of 2.3% in USD and 10.4% in INR terms. The sequential decline is 
because of deferred start and slower consumption of new projects. 
 
We reported a basic EPS of Rs. 34.1, up 8.3% compared to last year, and a diluted EPS of Rs. 33.9, 
up 8.4% compared to last year. EBITDA was down 100 bps sequentially, led by increments and 
ESOPs, which had a 190 bps impact, which was partially offset by AI-led productivity efficiency and 
additional working days. In Q2, the margin was on expected lines. Our endeavor will be to improve 
by at least 160 bps in the medium term. However, the velocity of improvement will be to some extent 
dependent upon macro and geopolitical factors. 
 
There were certain exceptional items during the quarter. We completed the sale of property in 
Chennai, resulting in a profit, which is reflected in exceptional items. The profit was offset by 
workforce restructuring cost due to AI-led efficiencies and write-off of old receivables in the book. 
This is one-time in nature. 
 
Now I'll move on to the cash position of the company. During Q2, we had another good collection 
quarter, wherein we collected $120 million from our customers, resulting in DSO of 74, a decrease 
of one day. A DSO of 74 days is one of the best in the industry, reflecting our current cash 
management and aggressive collection initiative. This also provides us with greater flexibility towards 
strategic decisions. 
 
The closing cash and investment balance net of debt is Rs. 582.7 crore. During the quarter, we paid 
a dividend of Rs. 50 crore plus loan repayment of around Rs. 55 crore. Despite that, we were able to 
add almost Rs. 36 crore to our net cash and investments. 
 
Now I'll move on to geography performance and industry-specific performance. All three 

geographies grew sequentially in Q1. UK continues to maintain a healthy EBIT of 18%. North America 
closed yet another quarter of healthy order book, as mentioned by Umang earlier, improving the total 
backlog position by 7.8% sequentially and 47.9% YoY. As mentioned by Umang, our AI momentum 
continues, and in this quarter, we closed 53 orders, which were AI deals, and almost 45% of the total 
order book were AI deals. 
 
In terms of industry, public sector business continued to show its strength by growing 6.1% 
sequentially, and private sector, namely Financial Services, grew by 15.3% sequentially. Utilization, 
including trainees, was down by 0.8% sequentially because of the investment we are making in 
domain resources. 
 
Now I'll talk about some other business parameters. During the quarter, we added 18 new customers, 
which was 13 in the previous quarter. Total closing headcount is 4,810, a reduction of 87 due to 
workforce restructuring and change in onsite/offshore mix. Our last 12-month attrition rate is down 
for the second consecutive quarter by 1.2%, from 16.4% to 15.2%. 
 
Lastly, I would like to call out some specific changes we have made in the Factsheet to better 
represent our performance. We have made few changes in client data to provide more meaningful 
representation of the business. This includes Active clients during the preceding 12 months, Active 
clients during the quarter, Forbes 1000 clients, Top 5 and Top 10 clients, Repeat business, and then 
we have made some changes in employee metrics by Segment and employee metrics by Time. 
 
With that, now I'll hand over the call to the operator who can open up for Q&A. Thank you so much. 
 
Moderator 
 
Thank you very much. We will now begin the question and answer segment.  
Our first question comes from Amit Chandra from HDFC Securities. Amit, please proceed with your 
question. 
 
Amit Chandra 
 
Thanks for the opportunity. My first question is on the order book. Obviously, you mentioned that we 
have been winning deals mostly AI-led. And also, we have been showing strong traction in terms of 
deal wins in the US geography. So the weakness in the order book is mostly led by slower execution 
in terms of the deals that we have won earlier. Or is it some kind of pressure we are seeing in the UK 
geography? And also, in terms of the commentary that FY27 will be better versus FY26, where do we 
stand on that? And some of the deals that we have won, what would be the ramp-up schedule for 
those deals? Thank you. 
 
Umang Nahata 
 
Thank you for your question, Amit. From the order backlog standpoint, there are two situations that 
we have. One, clearly, one of the large deals that we had won in North America last quarter with the 

federal government, the start of that deal has been currently delayed till post-midterm elections. And 
that has led to right-shifting of 12-month backlog numbers. That has caused some of the backlog to 
shift there. And similarly, there was also a deal in UK where we've already won the contract, but again, 
the consumption is slower than anticipated. We're hoping the consumption will pick up around Q4. 
And therefore, there also we've adjusted the 12-month backlog, looking at the slower consumption 
than anticipated. Having said that, we are still quite confident that we will be able to consume all of 
these orders, but the rate of consumption definitely is slower than expected. And like you said, that's 
one of the reasons why the 12-month backlog has seen a little softness in this quarter. 
 
On the second part of the question, Amit, as far as our forecast or our judgment that FY27 will be 
better than FY26, we continue to be optimistic that our H2 performance, there's no reason for it to 
be slower. We currently are positive that H2 should continue to do well. Having said that, some of 
the Middle East situation is definitely worrying and a little out of hand and out of control. And we've 
already seen a sizable dip in terms of Middle East performance to where we were hoping for. But 
currently, the UK and US are clearly managing that gap and therefore allowing us to deliver what we 
have to. So that's where the current situation is. From where we are, we feel comfortable that FY27 
will do better than FY26. But there are some of these geopolitical uncertainties and that is a little out 
of control for us. 
 
On an overall basis, the AI-native transformation is where we are also trying to adjust and pivot the 
organization to because those deals are consistently coming in, and the demand cycle on those is 
much stronger and much higher. As well as the execution is also much faster and better.  
 
Amit Chandra 
 
And some of the AI deals that we have won—are they coming from existing clients or are they coming 
from net-new clients? And also in terms of the size of these deals, where we see these sizes going 
on because most of the deals you mentioned are like smaller, project-based kind of deals. So when 
can we expect some large deal traction or some annuity kind of deals on the AI side? And also in 
terms of the overall revenue mix—if you can give what is the overall revenue from AI—and in terms 
of how the AI is growing YoY versus the non-AI part, it will be helpful for us to understand the mix. 
 
Umang Nahata 
 
Sure. So Amit, the AI deals are coming both from net-new customers and amongst the examples that 
I showed also today, at least two of those deals were net-new deals, which would not have been 
there if not for AI. So they are definitely net-new additions. Some of them are also with our existing 
customers where we are working with them to transform or improve productivity within their 
businesses. So it is definitely active both in terms of net-new as well as existing customer business. 
 
On the deal sizes of AI, I think they're currently running anywhere between $0.5 million to $5 million 
kind of deal size today in terms of AI. Some of the deals are even smaller, but those are like starting 
points, could be entry points, could be smaller. But average $0.5 million to $5 million is where we are 

currently seeing these deals. 
 
The AI transformative kind of deals, I believe initially would be small, but they'll be more evolving into 
larger deals instead of the customer signing one large deal at a go. We believe they'll sign 
transformation in pieces and you will keep evolving the business continuously. And that is our 
expectation from how these deals will move forward. So it might not land as one large order, but it 
will continue to evolve and grow into a stable, large, repeatable business within the same account 
and same project. 
 
As far as very large AI deals are concerned, the only area where we see them is if we're able to do an 
AI-led productivity takeout kind of work. And we are also pitching for those kinds of deals. We have 
quite a few of those deals in our pipeline today, but still to go out and execute and win some multi-
million dollar transactions. 
 
I gave you one example of the life sciences deal that we closed, which was a $10 million plus 
transaction. Again, an AI productivity kind of deal that we were able to execute. So AI productivity 
kind of takeouts are large, but AI transformative deals will still be under the $5 million bucket that I 
said. 
 
As far as the AI revenue and the sequential and consistent performance of AI from a revenue 
standpoint is concerned, we'll be starting to outline and present those numbers starting next quarter 
and onwards. So you will get a clear view of where those numbers are. But from where we see them, 
they are already contributing a significant percentage of our overall revenue. 
 
Amit Chandra 
 
Okay. And my last question on the margins. Obviously, the margins have been slipping down. So if 
you can provide the breakdown in terms of what actually led to the margin drop—in terms of what 
were the ESOP expenses plus the wage hike impact. And also you mentioned about 160 bps 
recovery in the medium term. So, if you can provide the bridge like what we have to watch out in 
terms of the margin trajectory. And also, in terms of the margins among various geographies, is it that 
the margins in the UK geography—which we are operating at the higher end, high teens—is there a 
risk of margins in the UK coming down because of productivity benefits demand? And also the 
margins trajectory for the US and the Middle East geography? Thank you. 
 
Deepak Kedia 
 
Hi Amit, Deepak this side I'll take this question. I'll take the questions in parts, and if I miss out on 
anything, do let me know, and I'll be happy to cover that as well. There are three parts to the margin 
drop. I think a couple of them you already highlighted. One is increment, and one is ESOP. Both 
combined, we have a 190 bps impact. 
 
Second impact which we are seeing in the business is basically a mix change. What I mean by mixed 
change is there are some large or high-margin projects which are ramped-down and replaced by low-

margin projects. The reason for the low margin was primarily sovereignty ask, and security cleared 
resource ask mainly in the UK territory. We have seen a drop in the margin in that particular segment. 
The impact of that is around 200 bps. 
 
Now, we have been able to drive a lot of AI-led efficiencies internally as well, and you would see I 
called out workforce restructuring costs as well because of that. That has given us an improvement 
of almost 200 bps. We are back to 150 to 160 bps drop from where we were, which was the 16% 
mark. That's basically the primary leverage. 
 
In current quarter, we did not have a significant forex impact, which typically is the case. That's 
possibly like a 20 bps tailwind which we got. In terms of future direction, we will have to go back to 
what we want to definitely go back to that 16% mark. Now, the velocity of how we can drive that will 
depend upon a lot of external factors. 
 
One factor which I said which basically has dropped the margin is the onsite mix wherein the ask for 
local security-cleared resources is definitely going up and localization is definitely going up. And we 
will have to deal with that and that will require a systematic change internally for us to basically 
recover that. There are plans in place internally. We have identified few areas which we are working 
on to basically improve the margin. 
 
Now, in the short-term to medium-term, as I said, the velocity will really depend upon how the macro 
factors move and if there are any changes in the current policies or the way the government is asking 
for security-cleared resources. We all know that our 60% - 65% of business comes from UK, which 
is primarily T&M. So, we'll have to abide by the rules which are given by the new government in UK. 
 
In terms of US and Middle East, we do definitely see an improvement in the margin space in both the 
geographies, starting Q3 itself. And that is definitely going to help us recover some of the margin 
which we have lost out in the UK because of the mix change. 
 
I hope Amit, I answered all your questions. If I missed any, please let me know. 
 
Amit Chandra 
 
No, it was helpful. Thank you, and all the best. 
 
Moderator 
 
Thank you. And our next question comes from Dipesh Mehta from Emkay Global. 
 
Dipesh Mehta 
 
Thanks for the opportunity. Just want to understand from a growth perspective, North America if I 
look at it, seems to be relatively muted. We were hopeful about growth rebounding in that geography. 
Can you help us understand which vertical is creating headwinds in that business? Because BFSI 

seems to be doing well, healthcare is where the weakness lies. If you can give some geographical 
angle to these two verticals, how both markets are playing out. 
 
Second thing is about AI. Some of the deals which you indicated about momentum and other things. 
Can you give some sense about whether you are observing size changes in some of those deals after 
the POC or maybe initial conversations and execution? Whether you are seeing size growing 
subsequently, and what kind of gross margin you make generally in those deals during subsequent 
execution? 
 
Thank you. 
 
Umang Nahata 
 
Thank you, Dipesh. As far as the North America business is concerned, like we've been saying over 
the last few quarters, the order book momentum clearly is moving in the right direction. And H2 is 
where we had predicted it will turn around, and we are sticking to that forecast that – North America 
business will start seeing meaningful turnaround from H2 in terms of its growth momentum. So, all 
the buildup that we've done for the last year or so—in terms of our order book, team structure, AI 
offerings, et cetera—has helped us create a strong base. And we believe starting H2, you should see 
a meaningful turnaround in North America from a growth standpoint. 
 
Healthcare & Life Sciences will continue to be our strongest vertical in North America, not just from 
a traditional business, but our AI focus is also very high on Healthcare & Life Sciences, including the 
Innovaccer partnership which is driving good positive momentum in terms of pipeline on AI 
transformation deals for Healthcare & Life Sciences in the geography. That's from the North America 
standpoint. 
 
As far as the AI deals are concerned, your observation is right. Especially the AI deals which start 
with POC or small use cases or transformation in one process area are leading into newer areas. So, 
as we deliver the transformation in one process area, it is opening up use cases for other areas to 
deliver transformation. Also, the potential of a solution to evolve is very, very high. And as the client 
sees benefit in the initial solution that we deliver to them, then there is an expanded scope of 
delivering similar kind of outcome or benefits in other areas of their business. So, we are continuously 
seeing that once the AI engagement starts in an account, it is clearly evolving into a continuous 
engagement of delivering more and more solutions. And it's not like a one-time, one-project kind of 
situation. 
 
From a margin standpoint on AI businesses, AI transformation or AI foundation kind of deals are 
running with a good margin of 40% plus gross margin and sometimes even running north of 50% plus 
gross margin kind of businesses. The AI productivity kind of deals are much more price aggressive, 
and we are clearly taking a very aggressive forward-looking three-year bet in terms of delivering 
anywhere between 35% to 60-70% productivity on some of our traditional IT services. In those deals, 
the margins are actually compressed. It will take time before we have upfront margin compression, 
but over a period of time, we'll be able to improve margins on these kinds of deals. That's where the 

AI margin story is. Hence, the focus is to move towards more and more transformation business, 
which is much sweeter in terms of Mastek’s capability than just compete on the AI productivity, 
which is clearly a red ocean. 
 
Dipesh Mehta 
 
I understand. And just on the vertical sense on the North America and UK market, if you can give 
some sense on BFSI particularly and healthcare, how those two markets played out in terms of 
growth trajectory? 
 
Umang Nahata 
 
So, BFSI, as I pointed out, continues to be a strong vertical for us. The BFSI growth is largely 
orchestrated by our UK-Europe business, where we are seeing really good traction. A lot of the work 
that we are doing is very modern data kind of work, which I pointed out earlier a couple of quarters 
back—the kind of deals that we had won with Bank of England and Financial Conduct Authority and 
a few others. And that deal momentum continues to do well. We're delivering some really good 
business value to these customers, and therefore continuing to grow the business in these accounts. 
 
The North America financial services market is also seeing good openings. We've opened a few 
interesting new logos in the geography. However, it needs still a lot of work to grow the Financial 
Services business in North America. We're still in the early stages. 
 
As far as Healthcare & Life Sciences is concerned, on the other hand, we are very strong on our 
capability both in North America as well as UK-Europe, and even in Middle East and APAC. And that 
is one of our strongest verticals and has a lot of focus and attention in really becoming an AI 
transformative partner for Healthcare & Life Sciences. A lot of the business that we are doing already
